transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-08
Start time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Alex Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Desai (Redwood SE), Martin Ortega (Fieldstone CISO), Leah Chan (Fieldstone Platform Eng), Raj Patel (Fieldstone Compliance)

Summary:
Quick sync to validate what admin events Redwood captures, how we can export/playback those logs for Fieldstone's forensics pipeline, discuss KMS options for envelope encryption, and agree on a short test for log replay into Fieldstone SIEM. Ask for SOC2 evidence pointers and SSO/RBAC mapping notes.

Topics:
- admin activity capture surface (who/what/actions)
- export formats and nearline storage (S3/Azure Blob)
- retention, lifecycle, and immutable snapshots
- KMS integrations (cloud KMS vs on-prem HSM)
- log playback/testing and PII redaction

Action items (captured in metadata too).

Transcript body:
[00:00] Alex Kim: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call please, and then we'll jump into the log playback demo.
[00:09] Martin Ortega: Martin here, CISO at Fieldstone. We got Leah and Raj too.
[00:13] Leah Chan: Yep Leah joining, hello.
[00:15] Raj Patel: Raj, compliance.
[00:17] Priya Desai: Priya from Redwood side, SE — I'll take the demo bits.
[00:22] Alex Kim: Perfect. Agenda is short: what we capture in admin events, how exports look, retention and lifecycle, and KMS. Then we want to schedule a hands-on replay test.
[00:31] Martin Ortega: Sounds good. Primary concern is we need immutable audit copies for a 7-year retention policy and ability to pull any admin action tied to a person or service account.
[00:40] Priya Desai: Totally understood. Quick note up front: our admin activity captures interactive console actions, API key ops, role changes, RBAC grants, and system-level escalations. There are also system-generated events like autoscaler changes and model route fallbacks but we can filter those.
[01:02] Raj Patel: When you say API key ops, does that include token creation and rotation events and IP allowlist changes? We need both creation and who triggered rotation.
[01:12] Priya Desai: Yes creation, rotation, revoke; and the event includes principal id, originating IP (sometimes proxied), timestamp, request id, and an opaque session id. IPs can be redacted on export if required but are captured initially.
[01:28] Leah Chan: What's the retention mechanism? Can we tier exports to our own bucket nightly? We don't want long tail sitting on Redwood for 7 years.
[01:36] Alex Kim: Two common patterns: Redwood offloads daily snapshots to customer-owned storage (S3/Azure Blob/GCS) via signed transfer or a push; or we provide a streaming export to your SIEM. For long-term immutable archives, the offload to your storage with object-lock is typical.
[01:55] Martin Ortega: Object-lock is important. Also need chain-of-custody metadata — we need to prove that the export wasn't altered. Do you sign exports?
[02:03] Priya Desai: We include an export manifest with checksums and a signed manifest (SHA256) and timestamp from our control plane. For Private deployments you can opt to sign with your KMS key as well, so it's double-signed.
[02:18] Martin Ortega: Double sign is good. For hosted customers, are those manifests accessible via an API?
[02:23] Priya Desai: Yes, the export job yields a presigned link plus a manifest endpoint you can query. We also keep an export history in the console.
[02:33] Raj Patel: On the export format, is it JSON-lines, CSV, or both? Our analysts prefer CSV for quick pivoting.
[02:40] Priya Desai: Primary format is newline-delimited JSON with a flattened schema; we also produce a CSV variant on request. The newline JSON keeps nested attributes (like request.headers) intact.
[02:52] Leah Chan: Can we request field-level redaction at export time? For example, scrub the prompt text in case PII was present?
[02:59] Priya Desai: You can configure redaction rules per export job or use our retention-based scrubber which redacts prompt/response content after X days. For compliance we normally recommend removing PII before shipping to SIEM, but you can also keep raw exports in your private bucket if you have strict access controls.
[03:17] Alex Kim: Quick interruption — Martin, are you evaluating hosted or private deployment for this workload?
[03:22] Martin Ortega: We're leaning hosted for now but might push to Private if we can't meet the long-term archival controls. Hosted is preferable for speed of onboarding.
[03:31] Priya Desai: Good to note. Hosted supports the same export features, but Private gives you more control over signing with your KMS/HSM.
[03:40] Leah Chan: About KMS, we run an on-prem HSM for key material. Can Redwood integrate with an on-prem HSM for export signing or envelope keys?
[03:48] Priya Desai: Yes, for Private deployments we support external KMS via KMIP and HSM connectors. For Hosted, we offer Customer-Managed Keys where you bring a cloud KMS, and we do envelope encryption. On-prem HSM direct attach is only available in Private.
[04:06] Martin Ortega: If we bring our cloud KMS (say, CloudVault), do you require key usage policies or just the key? I ask because we need enforcement that Redwood cannot export plaintext without us approving.
[04:17] Priya Desai: We require an asymmetric signing key for manifests or a symmetric envelope key for at-rest encryption. We never store your plaintext export if you configure customer-managed envelope. The service holds only the encrypted blobs and the envelope metadata; decryption requires the KMS call.
[04:33] Raj Patel: So retention: if we offload daily snapshots to our S3, can Redwood trigger lifecycle rules tagging to denote earliest retention start? We want a monotonic snapshot ID.
[04:42] Priya Desai: Each snapshot has a monotonically increasing export id, timestamp, and manifest. You can add lifecycle tags during the transfer and we can optionally call your lifecycle API to add retention tags.
[04:53] Leah Chan: For log playback, what's the fidelity? We want to replay admin events into our SIEM with original timestamps and correlate with other telemetry.
[05:01] Priya Desai: Exports include the original event timestamps and request ids. Our playback tool can stream the events preserving timestamps or we can produce a replay file with preserved timestamps. Caveat: if you want to re-ingest into a rate-limited SIEM, you'll want to throttle the playback — we provide a throttled streamer.
[05:19] Martin Ortega: Are there limits on how far back we can request point-in-time extracts? Like, suppose we wanted all admin events for March 2025 — can we pull that historically?
[05:28] Priya Desai: Retention on the Redwood side is configurable per account. For hosted, default is 90 days for active logs; we support on-request long-term snapshots if you arrange a snapshot export. For Private, you control that retention.
[05:42] Martin Ortega: Default 90 days is small. For our compliance we need 7 years. So plan is nightly offload to our S3.
[05:50] Alex Kim: Right — that's the recommended pattern. We'll demonstrate a nightly offload and object-lock configuration in the next call.
[05:57] Raj Patel: A couple of subtle asks: 1) we need to be able to link an audit record to the exact model version and compute instance that handled the request for forensic reconstruction; 2) we need RBAC mapping so our IdP groups map to Redwood roles.
[06:11] Priya Desai: For 1) we include model_id, model_version, and node_id in the event metadata. Node_id is anonymized unless you're on Dedicated or Private where we can expose instance ids. For 2) we support SAML and OIDC SSO, and you can map IdP groups to Redwood roles; we'll share the SSO mapping doc.
[06:30] Leah Chan: Node ids anonymized isn't perfect for us in hosted. If we need instance-level forensic we might need Private.
[06:36] Martin Ortega: Noted. Can you show a sample export manifest now?
[06:40] Priya Desai: Sure I'll paste a quick example — it's a newline json where each line has fields: timestamp, principal, action, resource, request_id, event_id, model_id, model_version, node_id (maybe null), ip, user_agent, payload_hash. Manifest contains file checksums and export_id.
[06:55] Alex Kim: (typing) I'm dropping a doc link in the chat: playbook/redwood-admin-export-sample — link.
[07:02] Martin Ortega: Got it. About encryption at rest for the exported files — if we push to our bucket, is the object encrypted during transfer and at rest?
[07:10] Priya Desai: Transfer uses HTTPS and pre-signed put with client-side TLS. For at-rest, if you use your bucket we rely on your bucket's encryption (SSE-KMS or SSE-C). If you want server-side encryption by Redwood, we can encrypt before transfer with customer-managed keys.
[07:26] Raj Patel: We need logs to include admin justification fields for manual approvals. Can manual approval steps be captured?
[07:33] Priya Desai: Yes manual approvals triggered via console produce approval events with approver id, approver comment, and approval outcome. Those are part of admin event schema.
[07:44] Leah Chan: For segregation of duties, can we have separate retention policies per role? For example, keep super-admin actions for longer.
[07:53] Priya Desai: Not out-of-box per role, but you can label events and set different export rules. We're discussing role-based retention in the roadmap — but the current approach is export-based tiering.
[08:06] Martin Ortega: Roadmap note appreciated. For evidence we need to pull a sample chain for a recent incident simulation. Could we run a replay for June 23rd actions?
[08:16] Priya Desai: Yes we can schedule a replay. I'll need a window of expected volume — we can throttle. Also we'll need destination details for your SIEM and temporary credentials if you want Redwood to push.
[08:29] Alex Kim: I'll capture that as an action item: Leah to share test window and SIEM endpoint.
[08:34] Leah Chan: I'll get that by Friday.
[08:36] Raj Patel: One more question on access control: Can you restrict Redwood employees from viewing exports or manifests? We need least privilege internally.
[08:45] Priya Desai: Yes, access is role-based; for hosted customers, only the account owner's admin role and designated support engineers can access exports. We have audit trails on export access; for additional assurance we can require that any support access is mediated through a short-lived access token that you approve.
[09:03] Martin Ortega: Support-mediated access is good. Also we need to validate that logs cannot be deleted without a multi-party approval. Is there a delete workflow?
[09:12] Priya Desai: Deletes are gated: if you request deletion, there's a retention check, and for hosted enterprise contracts we can require a multi-approver flow. For Private you can enforce harder controls.
[09:25] (short pause)
[09:29] Alex Kim: Let's talk about data residency: Fieldstone's legal team requires EU-only storage for EU accounts. How does export placement work across regions?
[09:38] Priya Desai: You can configure export endpoints per region. If the account is region-scoped, the default offload will write to a region-specific presigned link. For hosted multi-region setups we honor residency by only sending snapshots to buckets in the configured region.
[09:54] Leah Chan: Great. For the test, we'd like to see a replay preserving original timestamps and replay as if the events occurred at T. Does your replay tool have a 'preserve_time' flag?
[10:04] Priya Desai: Yes; preserve_time true will keep original timestamps in the payload. There's also a velocity control to slow playback for high-volume windows.
[10:12] Raj Patel: On the manifest signature: can we arrange to have the manifest signed by our KMS key after Redwood completes the export? That would prove chain-of-custody on our side.
[10:22] Priya Desai: For Private we'll support a post-export signing hook. For hosted we can invoke your KMS via a customer-managed key if you provide appropriate access. We'll include that as part of the integration checklist.
[10:36] Martin Ortega: Any limitations on exports for multi-tenant audit correlation? We might want to query cross-account events during incident triage.
[10:45] Priya Desai: Cross-account queries are limited for hosted due to tenant separation. We can produce aggregated reports for enterprise customers with multiple sub-accounts via an org-level export. But ad-hoc cross-account queries require enterprise enablement.
[11:00] Alex Kim: Switching gears — live demo: Priya, could you walk through a sample export job you've prepared?
[11:05] Priya Desai: Sure, I'm sharing my screen — note: screen transcription can be messy in the transcript. 
[11:12] [screen share noises] Priya Desai: Here's the export jobs panel, you can select date ranges, filters by principal, action types, and choose redaction presets. I'm selecting June 20-23 and enabling 'preserve_time' plus 'include raw payload'.
[11:30] Martin Ortega: Can you toggle redaction to hide prompt text and only include event metadata?
[11:36] Priya Desai: Clicking redaction preset 'PII-Strict' — now export will remove prompt/response fields and IPs. You can see a preview line: {timestamp: "2026-06-23T12:01:02Z", principal: "svc:analysis", action: "model.deploy", model_id: "rwd-emu-12", request_id: "req-abc123", payload_hash: "..."}.
[11:58] Leah Chan: That preview looks useful. Where does the playbook show the checksum and manifest signing?
[12:05] Priya Desai: Manifest panel shows file name, SHA256, export_id, signer: 'redwood-controlplane' and if you have customer signing enabled, we show 'customer-signer: cloudvault-key-01'.
[12:18] Raj Patel: A small nit — for compliance review we'd like a human-readable export report that maps event codes to compliance controls (e.g., ISO 27001 A.9.2). Is that something you can attach?
[12:29] Priya Desai: We can add a compliance mapping appendix to the manifest per request. It's manual today, but we have a template.
[12:36] Martin Ortega: Excellent. Couple more technical questions from Leah before we break: 1) Do backups of these exports end up in Redwood's backups? 2) If we rotate keys in our KMS, how do you re-key old exports?
[12:49] Priya Desai: 1) If exports are offloaded to your storage, Redwood does not keep long-term backups of those artifacts unless you request a copy. 2) For re-keying, we support re-encrypt operations where we pull the object, decrypt (if we have access via the KMS call), and re-encrypt with the new key; in Private you can do an offline re-wrap with your HSM. For hosted, re-key requires appropriate KMS permissions.
[13:08] Leah Chan: Okay that fits our model.
[13:11] (brief cross-talk)
[13:15] Alex Kim: Let's surface any blockers: Martin?
[13:18] Martin Ortega: The biggest blockers are 1) assurance that hosted will meet our 7-year legal retention without Redwood holding plaintext; 2) demonstration of manifest signing with our KMS; 3) the ability to map IdP groups to roles for separation-of-duty.
[13:33] Priya Desai: We can address 1 via nightly offload to your S3 with object-lock. For 2, we'll run a test where we trigger an export and call your KMS for signing in the pipeline; for hosted we need an IAM role with limited sign permission. For 3, SSO mapping doc will be shared and we can help configure claims mapping.
[13:53] Raj Patel: Timeline? We want a reproducible replay and manifest-signed export before the legal review on July 30.
[13:59] Alex Kim: Target: demo signed export and replay by July 22. Does that work?
[14:04] Martin Ortega: Yes, that gives us a week buffer.
[14:07] Leah Chan: I'll coordinate the replay test window and drop credentials for a test bucket.
[14:12] Priya Desai: Great. I'll also include a script snippet for how to validate manifest checksums locally and a small python sample to replay events into Splunk.
[14:23] Martin Ortega: Splunk yes, we'll test that. One smaller item: our legal might ask for an SLA clause guaranteeing export availability. Who would that be negotiated with?
[14:33] Alex Kim: Sales/legal will handle SLA amendments. I'll open an SOW thread and include the export availability commitments and manifest signing obligations.
[14:41] Raj Patel: On retention immutability, will you support WORM for exports initiated by Redwood?
[14:47] Priya Desai: We can set object-lock during the offload to your bucket if your storage supports it; Redwood will set retention metadata. For hosted we can't force your bucket's retention policy beyond setting the tag, but we can place objects with S3 object-lock if you give us the right policy.
[15:05] Alex Kim: We're about halfway — we still have time for a short Q&A and to confirm next steps.
[15:11] Leah Chan: Quick Q from me: does the export contain a canonical mapping to your RBAC roles for each event? I want a column that says 'redwood_role' for each principal so we can filter admin vs svc.
[15:21] Priya Desai: Yes we include resolved_role that maps the principal to the effective Redwood role at time of event. If there's a transient elevation, it's recorded as an elevation event with before/after roles.
[15:34] Martin Ortega: Good. Also want to make sure deletion of exports in our bucket doesn't automatically remove the export manifest from Redwood.
[15:41] Priya Desai: We retain export metadata in Redwood's control plane per your configured retention for the export history. Deleting the object from your bucket doesn't retroactively remove our metadata unless you request purge on both sides.
[15:53] Raj Patel: Any rate limits on export jobs? If we ask you to pull terabytes for a forensic case, what's the process?
[15:59] Priya Desai: For very large historical exports we do a manual offload job and coordinate throughput. We'll provide an estimated time based on size and can provide a direct transfer endpoint for high-volume pulls.
[16:12] Martin Ortega: Ok that helps. One last concern: can you attest that the events are tamper-evident once signed? We want to surface evidence to auditors.
[16:21] Priya Desai: The signed manifest plus checksum and optional KMS signature provides tamper evidence. We also append a control-plane audit trail entry when the export job transitions states. We can produce an auditor-facing report showing the workflow and signatures.
[16:38] (short pause)
[16:42] Alex Kim: Wrapping up — let's confirm action items and owners.
[16:46] Alex Kim: Action: Alex to send the pricing addendum and SOW draft for export SLA.
[16:51] Alex Kim: Action: Priya to share the KMS integration checklist, replay script, and sample export files.
[16:57] Alex Kim: Action: Leah to share test window, SIEM endpoint, and test bucket details.
[17:02] Alex Kim: Action: Martin to confirm whether Fieldstone will stay hosted or request Private by July 20.
[17:07] Martin Ortega: I'll aim to confirm by the 20th.
[17:10] Leah Chan: I'll send test details by Friday.
[17:13] Raj Patel: We'll review the SSO mapping doc when it's shared.
[17:17] Priya Desai: I'll post the artifacts to the thread and follow up with the replay instructions.
[17:21] Alex Kim: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up in email with links and the action matrix.
[17:26] (meeting ends)

Notes about transcript fidelity: occasional words may be mis-transcribed — node ids and keys may appear abbreviated. The demo included a screen share so a few visual notes were described in text.
